h.strategy: Borrow interaction patterns from other empirical sciences: epistasis in genetics (the effect of one mutation depends on genetic background, and beneficial mutations help fitter backgrounds less), diminishing returns in economics, and redundancy in engineered systems. Translate each pattern into a concrete conditional hypothesis about how an edit's effect varies with the parent configuration. Favor predictions that a practitioner thinking only mechanistically would get wrong, especially background-dependent sign changes and weaker gains in already-strong parents. Use conditions that many parents satisfy. In the flaw step, discard analogies that do not transfer and keep only those with a plausible general reason to hold.

hyps.why: A second conv path into node 3 is redundant when the direct edge 3 already carries a strong conv.
With a conv on the direct 0->3 edge, an extra conv on edge 5 adds little new capacity.
Two convs entering node 3 saturate, so the gain from edge 4 shrinks when edge 5 already has one.
Node 2 already receives conv features via the 0->1->2 route, so a conv on edge 1 is partly redundant.
Replacing a missing edge with a conv adds a whole new path, whereas replacing skip, pool or 1x1 only upgrades an existing one.
Downgrading a conv to skip loses more than setting skip over weaker ops such as pool or none.
A parallel identity path preserves the unblurred signal, so pooling on edge 4 hurts less.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 is dead and a conv on edge 2 has nothing to process.
Replacing a missing edge with a conv opens a new path, a larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Replacing a blurring pool with a learnable conv gains more than replacing an identity skip, which is already lossless.
